title: Infill housing and floodplain retail rezonings
subtitle: Also covered: private street names, parking restrictions on nine streets, and utility and receivable write-offs.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended two zoning changes. At 157 Schweitzer Street, it recommended rezoning to allow three new single-detached lots fronting Lark Street, with the existing house kept and tenants staying {{vote:m5}}. At 434-436 Queen Street South, it recommended adding retail as a permitted use in an existing floodplain building, with no changes to the building itself {{vote:m6}}.

On consent items, the committee recommended five private street names for a development at 995 Amand Drive {{vote:m1}}. It also recommended parking or stopping prohibitions on nine streets across the city {{vote:m2}}.
The committee also recommended writing off $121,784 in uncollectable utility accounts {{vote:m3}} and $12,341 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivables {{vote:m4}}.

These are recommendations to Council, which will make the final decisions. Residents near Schweitzer Street raised stormwater and electrical reliability concerns, which staff said will be reviewed at later stages.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended rezoning to RES-4 with a site-specific provision to allow three new two-storey single-detached lots on Lark Street while keeping the existing house {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended a site-specific floodplain zoning provision to add retail as a permitted use in the existing building {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended parking prohibitions on several street sections and weekday stopping prohibitions on Shea Crescent and Parkland Crescent, with the Uniform Traffic By-law amended accordingly {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended acknowledging five private street names (Amand Lane, Canyon Hill Drive, Sumac Lane, Azores Drive, Fig Lane) and directing Legal Services to prepare the by-law {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended writing off $121,784 in uncollectable utility accounts against the allowance for doubtful receivables {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended writing off $12,341 in uncollectable miscellaneous receivable accounts {{vote:m4}}.

debate: On Schweitzer Street, a councillor asked the applicant's planner whether a 2-metre rear and side fence would be acceptable to address neighbours' privacy and overlooking concerns. The planner had no objection. Staff said the Planning Act sections used for this approval do not allow such a condition, so it could only be offered in good faith. The councillor said they would follow up with staff before Council.

Neighbours' main concerns were stormwater drainage and electrical reliability. Staff said the Lark Street storm sewer is shallow, but options such as infiltration galleries or rear-yard infiltration will be reviewed at the later consent stage. The local utility reported no capacity issues in the area.

Councillors asked about sidewalks and snow clearing, since the area has no sidewalks. The applicant's planner said each 9-metre lot would leave room beside the driveway for a walkway and snow storage. Another councillor questioned why the Region collects a fee when it is barely involved in this application. Staff said the Region would need to answer that.

On Queen Street South, a councillor asked why the report did not mention the heritage district. Staff said no exterior changes or additions are proposed, so no heritage concerns were raised. Staff also said any future expansion would need a heritage permit and Grand River Conservation Authority approval.

The Queen Street South application was a one-time, no-fee floodplain rezoning. The Grand River Conservation Authority had no objection because it would not increase flood risk. The applicant said the intended retail use was a vape store, not cannabis.
